beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Limits of Machine Intelligence examines what impossibility theorems do, and do not, forbid.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It distinguishes a universal decision procedure from bounded certificates for a particular operating envelope.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book develops this distinction through the exploratory philosophy of outfinitism.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It preserves classical limits while asking where boundary detection and suspended judgment become useful.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers can evaluate a proposed framework without treating it as an established mathematical foundation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A finite operating domain can permit exhaustive checking while remaining computationally impractical.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some diagonal limits still apply because their transformations use finite descriptions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book therefore distinguishes logical possibility from feasible verification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Outfinitism asks what a finite agent is entitled to claim at its current frontier.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its vocabulary is a proposal whose usefulness must be demonstrated.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A certificate depends on assumptions about its domain, resources, precision, and operating conditions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Moving beyond those conditions requires justification for carrying the result forward.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book treats boundary detection, fallback, cost, and unresolved status as substantive obligations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Existing verification techniques supply important comparisons rather than being displaced by a new name.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This makes the proposed philosophy answerable to actual assurance problems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the distinction between global impossibility and a particular bounded claim.
